angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 221,928 km at 66.89 pc = 0.04 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 14.9490 +/- 0.0222 mas (same row, RUWE 1.09): 66.89 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 0.319 +/- 0.018 solar radii from Scott et al. 2026, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of TOI-7384 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2026MNRAS.547ag070S/abstract): 221,928 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.318 +/- 0.016 solar masses from Scott et al. 2026, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of TOI-7384 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2026MNRAS.547ag070S/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 3185 +/- 75 K from Scott et al. 2026, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-7384 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2026MNRAS.547ag070S/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Scott et al. 2026, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-7384 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2026MNRAS.547ag070S/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/toi-7384.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.933, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, coloured from a blackbody at the star's published temperature (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
